note:
**The 1921 census - Barrack Lane, Allenfield Lodge and 9 Cavendish Crescent South.** Schedules 75 and 212 to 221, read from the householders' own schedules by A. Hagues. **Nine houses the record held nothing for in 1921.**

**The run places itself at both ends.** The 1921 schedule asks for each person's **place of work**, and a domestic servant's place of work is the house she lives in. Schedule 212 gives **16 Barrack Lane** against Florence Taylor, and schedule 216 gives **26 Barrack Lane** against Alice Richmond. With both ends fixed by the page itself, the three between them follow in schedule order at 18, 20 and 22 - and 24, which the record holds for 1911, is passed over.

| schedule | house | head | in the house |
|---|---|---|---|
| 212 | **16 Barrack Lane** | Ernest William Topham, lace manufacturer | 3 |
| 213 | **18 Barrack Lane** | Frederick W Pare, lace manufacturer | 8 |
| 214 | **20 Barrack Lane** | Alfred Pike, hosiery underwear manufacturer | 6 |
| 215 | **22 Barrack Lane** | Joseph T Darby, china and glass dealer, retired | 4 |
| 216 | **26 Barrack Lane** | Elizabeth Bradwell, widow of 74 | 3 |
| 217 | **28 Barrack Lane** | Margaret Hannah Johnson, widow | 4 |
| 218 | **30 Barrack Lane** | Alfred Harwood, insurance district manager | 6 |
| 221 | **Allenfield Lodge** | Maurice Mee, machinist and driller | 6 |
| **75** | **9 Cavendish Crescent South** | **Stephen Cecil Armitage**, solicitor and employer | 3 |

**Schedule 75 places itself too.** Lilian Ivy Cross, the maid, gives her place of work as **9 Cavendish Crescent South, The Park**. The house held only 1911 before this. Her master is **thirty-one and already an employer**; his wife Ellen Louisa Alexander Armitage was born at Pontypool and is **twenty-three**, and the schedule records no children.

**Schedule 218 places itself the same way** - Maggie Quincey's place of work is written **30 Barrack Lane**. With 212 at 16, 218 at 30 and 216 at 26, three points of the run are fixed by the page and the rest follow the schedule numbers.

**Allenfield Lodge is filed to Barrack Yard.** The record has no property of that name and the Yard is what stands at that end of the lane; the page's own words are kept in every source line and in a `source_address` on every row, so nothing is lost if the two turn out to be different places.

**32 and 34 Barrack Lane are in the run and not in the record.** Schedules 219 and 220 sit between 30 and Allenfield Lodge, and the property list stops at 30. Those two houses want creating when the schedules are read.

Every enumerator's total checks - persons, males and females alike.

## What the 1921 columns give that no earlier round does

**Ages in years and months**, so every one of these forty people has their birth month as well as their year. The record holds the years; the months are in the source lines.

**Employer and place of work by name.** Ernest William Topham works at **Sellarts Factory, Beeston** and **Holland Street**. Frederick W Pare and his son John run **John Pare & Son, lace manufacturers, Russell Street** - the son, at twenty, is already assistant manager. Alfred Pike employs two of his own children at **Argyle Street Works**: Ernest Henry as a hosiery mechanic and Gladys Winifred as a clerk. Herbert Bradwell practises as a solicitor on his own account at **10 Park Row**.

**Elizabeth Pare, sister to Frederick, was born at Calais** and is entered as British born - the schedule has a column for it.

**Margaret Johnson of 28 Barrack Lane is a riding mistress**, twenty-seven, and an **employer**, with her place of work at Edwalton. **Alfred Harwood** manages insurance districts for the County Fire Office and the Alliance Assurance Company from Exchange Walk, and his son audits for Leman Hill & Hilton. **Maurice Mee** is a machinist and driller at the **Raleigh Cycle Works**, with a daughter machining hosiery and a son clerking for Moore & Morell.

## Two readings left as they stand

Florence Taylor at 16 Barrack Lane is **seventeen years and ten months old and entered as Married**. It may be the enumerator's slip and it may not. The record keeps what the page says and says so here.

The head of schedule 221 is entered as **Father**, not Head, and the schedule carries no signature. Maurice Mee is plainly the man keeping the house, and the record treats him as the head, but the column says what it says.
